verdict.summary: Critic 3.9/10 — first impression 5, world 4, legibility 3, automation 3, heat 6, night 3, onboarding 6, feel 4, coherence 3, keep-playing 2. Blind: OURS 0, EVEN 2 (information design, pressure and consequence), THEIRS 8, four of them "by a lot". Pressure and consequence rose to EVEN — F2s gunnery and toll work landed. Everything about looking at the game fell.
verdict.biggest_gap: YOU CANNOT SEE THE NIGHT, AND THE PREVIOUS FIX WAS AIMED AT THE WRONG VARIABLE. sprite_factory _hide() clamps all eleven enemy kinds to RGB about (14,11,16) — 5% luminance — on a night ground the post grade puts at 12-18%. The silhouette is DARKER than the background it sits on. A gamma-0.35 lift of the whole frame finds zero enemies while the renderer reports 27 agents drawn that tick. The previous pass answered the same finding by raising MIN_AGENT_PX from 17 to 24 — size, not contrast. And the instrument that should have caught it is blind too: --ui-tour fails 11 of 17 with all eleven screenshots being the main menu, the same title-screen blindness fixed in frame_lab one wave ago and never fixed here.
